paper_title: Cosmological bounds on pseudo Nambu-Goldstone bosons
notes: ALP two-photon coupling; paper Eq.(1.1) L=-(g/4)F Ftilde phi matches the canonical g_agamma normalisation, so no conversion (g=g_agamma). Figure 1 (m_phi vs g) is a summary plot combining ~12 overlapping cosmological+astro bounds forming one large excluded blob that touches the plot top (m<~1e5 eV, via HB/lab overlays from other refs) and bottom (m>~1e2 eV), so there is no single clean headline curve. Reported curve = lower (exclusion-reach) boundary of the N_eff excluded region (yellow in Fig.1 / Fig.6), which the paper states is its most relevant original contribution (Sec.1: N_eff bound is the most relevant and covers most of parameter space). N_eff occupies the small-coupling/large-lifetime edge, so its lower boundary is the frontier; extracted from the yellow filled band (m~1e5-3e8 eV) plus its dashed continuation (to ~1e11 eV), pixel-traced from the rendered PDF figure and made monotone-descending (a ~1-decade band-to-dashed-line join artifact near 3e8 eV was smoothed by a running-min envelope). Calibration cross-checked with tau=64pi/(m^3 g^2) (Eq.1.2): mid-mass point gives tau~1e2 s (BBN era) as expected. Astrophysical HB and SN regions (blue/cyan, from other references) excluded. BBN bounds quoted at 95% C.L. (Yp<0.2631, D/H). CAVEAT: if the compilation digitised the combined cosmology region outer boundary rather than the N_eff sub-bound, this curve is a lower-edge subset; hence moderate confidence.
